name: dinoctor-mcp

tools.name: open_dinoctor
tools.description: Start the Dinoctor app on this computer if it isn't open, and wait (up to about 90 seconds) until its window is ready. Call this first. Returns { opened, ready }. Fails with a download hint if the app isn't installed. To only check whether it's open, use status.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Quick read-only check: is Dinoctor open, the project's style and format, how many scenes and shots, and which shot is on screen (id and indexes). Returns { open: false, note } when the app is closed. For every scene and shot, use get_project.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Read-only: the whole project in short form. Style, format, and every scene and shot with id, index, length, camera, place, cast (member ids and refs), number of actions, texts and transition. Read it before editing to get the ids other tools need (shot_id, member ids). For every setting of one shot use get_shot; for a picture use look_at_shot.

tools.name: get_shot
tools.description: Read-only: every setting of one shot as JSON (place, cast, actions, emotions, texts, camera and camera keys, lighting, transition, keyframes), with its scene and shot index. Name the shot with shot_id, or scene and shot indexes; left out, the shot on screen. Use it to see exact fields and ids before edit_project or set_keyframes. For a short view of all shots use get_project; to see the shot as a picture use look_at_shot.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

tools.name: go_to
tools.description: Show a shot in Dinoctor's editor so the person sees what you're working on. Name it with shot_id, or scene and shot indexes. Changes only what's on screen, not the project. Edit tools use the shot on screen when no shot is given, so this also sets their default. Returns { showing }. To get a picture of the shot, use look_at_shot.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

tools.name: edit_project
tools.description: Low-level edit of any project setting by JSON Pointer path (read how_to once for the format, get_shot for a real shot). Each change: {"op":"replace"|"add"|"remove"|"merge","path":"/scenes/0/shots/1/seconds","value":4}. All changes in one call are one undo step; a bad path or value is refused and nothing changes. Returns { done: number of changes }. Prefer the specific tools (set_cast, direct_cast, set_text, set_camera, set_light, set_place, set_transition, set_keyframes); use this only for fields they don't cover.

op.description: replace a value, add one (append to a list with path ending '-'), remove it, or merge fields into an object.

path.description: JSON Pointer into the project, like "/scenes/0/shots/1/seconds".

value.description: The new value. Not needed for remove.

changes.description: The changes, applied in order as one undo step.

label.description: What the person sees in the undo note, like 'Claude made shot 2 longer.'

tools.name: new_project
tools.description: Replace the open project with a new, empty one (one scene, one shot with the style's start place, light and lead character). The first call only says what will happen; ask the person, then call again with confirm: true. The person can Undo it right after. To keep the project and only change its look, use set_style; to open a saved file, use open_project. Returns the new scene and shot ids.

style.description: Style id from list_styles, like pixel, toon, voxel, docu. Left out: the current style.

format.description: horizontal 16:9 or vertical 9:16. Left out: the current format.

confirm.description: true only after the person said yes.

tools.name: set_style
tools.description: Switch the whole project to another built-in art style. Every shot is rebuilt from the new style's own place, light and lead character: actions, cast, scenery and keyframes go; texts and lengths stay. If the project already has work, the first call returns needsConfirm; ask, then call with confirm: true. One undo step for the person. For one of the person's own styles use use_style; to start fresh use new_project.

confirm.description: true only after the person agreed to rebuild the shots.

tools.name: set_format
tools.description: Make the whole video horizontal (16:9, YouTube) or vertical (9:16, Reels / Shorts / TikTok). Shots stay as they are, framed for the new shape. One undo step for the person. Returns { done } with the ids of what changed.

tools.name: add_scene
tools.description: Add a scene (a group of shots, usually a new place or moment) with one shot in it, and show it. The shot starts like the app's + Scene: the last shot's place, light and cast (or the style's plain place), a still medium camera, 3 seconds. Returns the new scene id, shot id and cast ids. One undo step for the person. To add a shot to an existing scene, use add_shot.

name.description: Like 'The chase'. Left out: Scene N.

after.description: Scene id or index to put it after. Left out: after the last scene.

seconds.description: Length of its first shot in seconds (3 if left out).

place.description: Place preset id. Ids must come from the current style: call library to see them (a wrong id is refused with the valid list).

empty.description: true: start with nobody in the shot.

tools.name: add_shot
tools.description: Add one empty shot (no cast, no scenery items; place, light and look carry on from the shot before, like the app's + Shot). By default it goes right after the shot on screen. Returns the new shot id. Then fill it with set_cast, direct_cast, set_text, set_camera, set_light, set_place and set_transition. One undo step for the person. For a new place or moment use add_scene; to copy a shot use duplicate.

after.description: Put it right after this shot id.

scene.description: Or: add it at the end of this scene (id or index).

first.description: With scene: put it first in the scene instead.

seconds.description: Length in seconds (3 if left out).

place.description: Place preset id, with its scenery. Ids must come from the current style: call library to see them (a wrong id is refused with the valid list).

tools.name: remove
tools.description: Remove a shot (shot_id, or scene + shot) or a whole scene (scene alone, or its id). A scene's only shot can't be removed alone (remove the scene), and the last scene can't go. One undo step for the person. Returns { done }. To take a person or object out of a shot, use set_cast with op remove.

shot_id.description: A shot's id from get_project.

scene.description: Scene index from 0. Alone: the whole scene; with shot: that shot.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

id.description: Or: a shot id or a scene id from get_project.

tools.name: move
tools.description: Move a shot (shot_id) to another position, in its own scene or into another scene (scene is where it goes). The shot keeps all its settings. One undo step for the person. Returns { done, shot }. To copy instead of move, use duplicate.

shot_id.description: The shot to move (its id from get_project).

scene.description: Target scene id or index. Left out: its own scene.

before.description: Put it before this shot id.

index.description: Or: its new position in the scene, from 0. Left out (and no before): the end.

tools.name: duplicate
tools.description: Copy a shot (shot_id, or scene + shot; the copy goes right after it) or a whole scene (scene alone, or its id; the copy goes after it). Copies are separate: changing one never changes the other. Returns the new ids. One undo step for the person. For a new empty shot use add_shot.

shot_id.description: A shot's id from get_project.

scene.description: Scene index from 0. Alone: the whole scene; with shot: that shot.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

id.description: Or: a shot id or a scene id from get_project.

tools.name: cut_shot
tools.description: Cut a shot (shot_id, or scene + shot; left out: the shot on screen) in two at a time, like a clip in an editor: both parts together play exactly what the shot played; the second keeps the transition and the voice stays in the first. Times round to 0.1 s and must be at least 0.2 s from either edge. Returns { first, second } shot ids. One undo step for the person. To change only the length, use edit_project on seconds.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

at.description: Seconds into the shot where it's cut.

tools.name: rename_scene
tools.description: Rename a scene (the name the person sees in the scene list and the timeline). Names don't have to be unique and change nothing else in the film. One undo step for the person. Fails if the scene isn't found or the name is empty. Returns { done }. Shots have no names; scenes are listed by get_project.

name.description: The new name, like 'The chase'. Short is best; it can't be empty.

tools.name: set_cast
tools.description: Add, change or remove a character or object in a shot (shot_id, or scene + shot; left out: the shot on screen). op add needs ref (a character or object id of the style); change and remove need member (its id from get_shot, or its name). Ids must come from the current style: call library to see them (a wrong id is refused with the valid list). A character added without x is spaced out automatically. Returns the shot and member ids. One undo step for the person. To make the cast move or feel something, use direct_cast; for animation over time, use set_keyframes.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

ref.description: Character or object id (add), or a new one of the same kind (change swaps it).

name.description: A name for this member, like 'Mia'. Used by direct_cast and in undo notes.

x.description: Left (-) to right (+); about -8 to 8 is in frame.

z.description: Near (+) to far (-); 0 is the front line.

y.description: Height above the ground; 0 stands on it.

turn.description: Degrees, turning round like on a stage.

spin.description: Degrees, turning in the picture like a wheel.

accessory.description: hat, crown, party, bow (only characters that can dress), or "".

pose.description: A pose id the character offers.

auto_x.description: change: true lets the scene space it out again.

tools.name: direct_cast
tools.description: Direct the cast of a shot (shot_id, or scene + shot; left out: the shot on screen): actions, faces, talking and looking. kind action: a move (type from library actions) by actor, some need a target; timed by when or exact at %. kind emotion: a face feeling on member at %. kind talk: member's mouth moves from % to %. kind look: member looks at target from % to %. op add (default), change (id), remove (id), clear (all of that kind). Ids must come from the current style: call library to see them (a wrong id is refused with the valid list). Returns the item id. One undo step for the person. To place or remove people use set_cast; for exact paths over time use set_keyframes.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

op.description: add if left out. clear removes every item of this kind in the shot.

id.description: The action/emotion/talk/look id, for change and remove.

actor.description: Member id or name doing the action (first cast member if left out).

target.description: Member id or name it's done to / looked at.

member.description: For emotion, talk, look: whose face.

when.description: Rough timing in the shot. Use at for an exact %.

at.description: When it happens, in % through the shot (0 to 100)

from.description: Start, in % through the shot (0 to 100)

to.description: End, in % through the shot (0 to 100)

tools.name: set_text
tools.description: Add, change or remove on-screen text in a shot (shot_id, or scene + shot; left out: the shot on screen). preset is one of the style's text presets (its look and font); action is its animation (pop, slam, type, fade, slide, drop...). Ids must come from the current style: call library to see them (a wrong id is refused with the valid list). Returns the shot and text ids. One undo step for the person. For a script line that is spoken, use script with action write or assign (its captions come from the voice).

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

id.description: Text id, for change and remove.

words.description: The text. Short reads best: 2 to 5 words.

when.description: Rough timing in the shot. Use at for an exact %.

x.description: Centre across, in % of the frame (50 is the middle).

y.description: Centre down, in % of the frame (18 is near the top; captions sit near 84).

at.description: When it appears, in % through the shot (0 to 100)

until.description: When it leaves, in % through the shot (0 to 100)

line_words.description: Words per line (2 if left out).

font.description: A font family the style offers, or "".

tools.name: set_camera
tools.description: Set a shot's camera (shot_id, or scene + shot; left out: the shot on screen): a preset move with strength and wiggle, or direct it with camera keys (keys win over the move). Each key: at (seconds) and any of x, y, z, distance, height, angle, roll, ease; what a key leaves out is taken from where the camera is at that moment. Ids must come from the current style: call library to see them (a wrong id is refused with the valid list). Returns the camera settings. One undo step for the person. For the end-of-shot camera move into the next shot, use set_transition (outro_camera).

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

move.description: Camera move id (library cameras). Clears camera keys.

strength.description: How far the move goes, 0 to 100.

wiggle.description: Handheld feel: 0 locked off, 1 normal, up to 3.

z.description: Point it looks at: near (+) / far (-).

distance.description: Distance from that point, about 2 to 40.

roll.description: Tilt of the picture, about -3.2 to 3.2.

ease.description: smooth, even, fast-start, slow-start, punch, bounce

still.description: true on a single key: a locked camera that doesn't move.

replace_keys.description: false: add these keys to the ones there. Default replaces them.

clear_keys.description: true: drop camera keys, back to the move.

tools.name: set_light
tools.description: Light a shot (shot_id, or scene + shot; left out: the shot on screen): a lighting preset (the style's moods), and/or the ambient colour and level, and single lights. Any hand change makes it a custom look. Ids must come from the current style: call library to see them (a wrong id is refused with the valid list). Returns the lighting. One undo step for the person. To change the light over time, use set_keyframes (scene:light or light:<id>).

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

tools.name: set_place
tools.description: Set where a shot happens (shot_id, or scene + shot; left out: the shot on screen): a place preset (with its scenery), and/or its colours and sky, and scenery items. Ids must come from the current style: call library to see them (a wrong id is refused with the valid list). Returns the place and its item ids. One undo step for the person. For a generated photo background use generate_picture with kind background; for your own picture use upload with as background.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

kind.description: An object or place id of the style.

tools.name: set_keyframes
tools.description: Animate anything in a shot (shot_id, or scene + shot; left out: the shot on screen) by hand with keyframes on a track. Tracks: "cast:<member id>" (x, y, z, size, spin, turn), "item:<item id>" (x, z, size), "text:<text id>" (x, y, size), "light:<light id>" (x, y, z, intensity, color), "scene:light" (level, ambient), "mask:shot", "adjust:<group>", "element:<id>". op set puts values at a time (a first key after 0 also keys the resting value at 0), remove deletes the key at that time, clear drops the track. One undo step for the person. For ready-made moves use direct_cast; for the camera use set_camera keys.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

track.description: Which thing, like "cast:member-1" or "scene:light" (ids from get_shot).

ease.description: How it travels on to the next key: smooth, even, fast-start, slow-start, punch, bounce.

tools.name: set_transition
tools.description: Set how a shot (shot_id, or scene + shot; left out: the shot on screen) changes into the next one: a transition id (cut, fade, whip-left, match-zoom-in, ink-splat... see library transitions), its length, and its options. Also the end-of-shot moves before it (outro camera, effect, character), or a ready combo of both. Empty string removes an outro part. Ids must come from the current style: call library to see them (a wrong id is refused with the valid list). Returns the transition. One undo step for the person.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

color.description: For transitions that use a colour: "#RRGGBB".

word.description: For transitions that show a word.

point.description: For transitions that start at a point: [across, down], 0 to 1.

outro_camera.description: Outro camera move id, or "" to remove.

outro_effect.description: Outro effect id, or "" to remove.

outro_character.description: Outro character move id, or "" to remove.

outro_ref.description: Which character id does the outro move.

outro_size.description: Size of that character, 1 is normal.

tools.name: list_styles
tools.description: Read-only: every built-in Dinoctor style with its id, name, what it's for and its depth (2D, 2.5D or real 3D), with the project's current style marked. Use an id with library (what it offers), new_project or set_style. The person's own styles are listed by my_styles.

tools.name: library
tools.description: Read-only: the ids a style offers, by category (characters, objects, places, cameras, actions, emotions, text_presets, text_animations, transitions and outro moves, lights, looks, elements, samples), with names and short notes. With no category and no search it returns counts only; pass category and/or search to keep answers small. Every id you pass to set_cast, direct_cast, set_text, set_camera, set_light, set_place or set_transition must come from here. For ready-made shot recipes to add, use samples.

style.description: A style id from list_styles. Default: the project's style.

category.description: One of: characters, objects, places, cameras, actions, emotions, text_presets, text_animations, transitions, lights, looks, elements, samples.

search.description: Words to look for in id, name, group and note, like 'zoom' or 'sad'.

tools.name: how_to
tools.description: Read-only reference text: the project format (Project > Scene > Shot fields), units (seconds vs percent), x/z ranges and keyframe tracks. Read it once before using edit_project. It doesn't need the app open. For the drawing format of draw, use draw with action describe.

tools.name: look_at_shot
tools.description: See a shot: returns a picture (about 960 px wide) of a shot at a moment, plus its info, so you can check what you made and fix it. Use it after changes. Give a shot (shot_id, or scene and shot index; default the shot on screen) and seconds into it, or film: true with seconds into the whole film. It shows that shot in the editor and pauses it; the project isn't changed. Doesn't work while a render runs. For the shot's settings as data use get_shot; for a video file use render.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

seconds.description: Seconds into the shot (or the film with film: true). Default 0.

film.description: true: seconds counts from the start of the whole film.

width.description: Picture width in pixels, 240 to 1920. Default 960.

tools.name: render
tools.description: Make a video file of the film, one scene or one shot, the same way Export does, and follow or stop it. action start (default): starts the render and returns at once; it gives no file yet. action status (read-only): stage, progress (0 to 1), frames and seconds so far; when done, the file path; or the error. Call it every 10 to 30 seconds while running. action cancel: stops the running render (no file is made; safe when nothing runs). Only one render runs at a time, and look_at_shot doesn't work while it runs. quality draft is 540p and quick (for checking timing); final is full size and much slower. make wav or mp3 exports only the sound. Without save_to it goes to Dinoctor's renders folder.

action.description: start (default) a render, status of the render, or cancel it.

what.description: start: what to render. Default film (shot when shot_id is given).

shot_id.description: start: a shot id to render that shot.

id.description: start: a scene id (what: scene) or shot id (what: shot).

scene.description: start: scene index from 0 (what: scene or shot).

shot.description: start: shot index from 0 in that scene (what: shot).

blur.description: Motion blur for final (about 4 times slower). Default on where possible.

save_to.description: Full path of the file to make, ending in .mp4 (or .wav/.mp3). Ask the person where if they care.

replace.description: Write over save_to if it's already there.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Read-only: the person's recent project files (path, name, style, when opened, whether the file still exists), and which file is open now and whether it has unsaved changes. Use a path with open_project.

tools.name: open_project
tools.description: Open a project file (.dino) in Dinoctor, the same as File > Open, in place of the open project. Refuses if the open project has unsaved changes, unless discard: true (ask the person first, or save_project before). Returns the opened project's summary. For a new empty project use new_project; for a template use templates.

path.description: The project file's full path (see list_projects).

discard.description: true: drop unsaved changes in the open project. Only after the person agreed.

tools.name: save_project
tools.description: Save the open project to a .dino file, the same as File > Save. With path: Save As to that file. With name: a new file with that name in the person's projects folder. A project never saved before gets a file in the projects folder. Returns the file path. To save it as a reusable starting point, use templates with save.

name.description: A name for a new file in the projects folder.

tools.name: generator_account
tools.description: Read-only check of the paid services Dinoctor can use and what's left: Higgsfield (pictures: signed in, credits, any job running), ElevenLabs (voices: connected, plan, characters left) and whether Claude Code is here (for writing scripts). Call it before paid tools to see if they will work. sign_in: true opens the person's browser to sign in to Higgsfield themselves.

sign_in.description: true: open the person's browser at the Higgsfield sign-in page. Only when they asked to sign in.

tools.name: generate_picture
tools.description: Make a picture with Higgsfield (Nano Banana) from words, and follow or stop the job. action make (default): kind character or object (whole body, its background is taken off) or background (a place, no people); put says where it goes: shot (a character or object joins the shot's cast, or replaces a member's picture with replace; a background becomes the shot's place), media (the Media bin, the default) or none (only the generated pictures list). Spends the person's Higgsfield credits: the first call (without confirm) only returns the price and credits left; ask the person, then call again with the same arguments and confirm: true. Waits up to about 50 s; if it isn't done, call generate_picture with action status. action status: waits up to wait seconds for the picture being made (by make or relight) and, when it's done, puts it where that call said and returns its id; { done: false } with the stage while it works, { job: null } when nothing is being made. action stop: stops the picture being made. For a free drawing in the style itself use draw; to reuse a picture made before use put_picture (list them with generated_pictures).

action.description: make (default) a new picture, status of the one being made, or stop it.

kind.description: make: character or object (background taken off), or background (a place, no people). Needed for make.

prompt.description: What to draw, in plain words. @1, @2 point at the reference pictures in order.

references.description: Paths of up to 4 pictures on this computer to keep the same person or thing.

from_pictures.description: Ids of pictures made before (generated_pictures) to use as references.

confirm.description: true only after the person agreed to the price.

put.description: Where it goes: shot (into the shot), media (the project's Media bin), none (only the generated pictures list).

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

replace.description: A cast member id in that shot whose picture this replaces.

name.description: A short name for it in the project.

wait.description: status: seconds to wait for it, 0 to 110. Default 50.

tools.name: generated_pictures
tools.description: Read-only list of pictures made with Higgsfield before (kept on this computer for every project), newest first: id, kind, what was asked, when, folder. Free to reuse: pass an id to put_picture, remove_background, relight, or as from_pictures in generate_picture. Pictures already in the project are in get_shot instead.

limit.description: Most pictures to list, 1 to 100. Default 30.

tools.name: put_picture
tools.description: Put a picture made before (an id from generated_pictures) into the project, free: as a character or object (joins a shot's cast, or replaces a member's picture), a background (the shot's place) or media (the Media bin). One undo step. Returns where it went. For a file on this computer use upload; for a new picture use generate_picture.

as.description: How it goes into the project.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

replace.description: A cast member id in that shot whose picture this replaces.

name.description: A short name for it in the project.

tools.name: remove_background
tools.description: Take the background off a picture made before (generated_pictures id) with Higgsfield's remover; the saved picture is changed. Uses a little of the person's Higgsfield credits: the first call only says so; call again with confirm: true after they agree. Optionally puts the result into a shot or the Media bin (as). For free trimming, cropping or flipping of a picture already in a shot, use cutout.

confirm.description: true only after the person agreed to spend the credits.

as.description: Where to put the cut-out; leave out to only change the saved picture.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

replace.description: A cast member id in that shot whose picture this replaces.

tools.name: relight
tools.description: Higgsfield relights a picture photo-real: everything stays, only the light changes (like the Thumbnail studio's Make it real). Give a picture file path or a generated picture id, and the light in words. A new picture is made; the original stays. Spends the person's Higgsfield credits: the first call (without confirm) only returns the price and credits left; ask the person, then call again with the same arguments and confirm: true. Waits up to about 50 s; if it isn't done, call generate_picture with action status. The result goes to media, a shot's background, or nowhere. To light a shot in the app itself (free), use set_light.

path.description: Full path of a PNG, JPG or WebP on this computer. Or give id.

id.description: A generated_pictures id instead of a path.

light.description: The light, like 'warm low sun from the left, soft blue fill'.

confirm.description: true only after the person agreed to the price.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

tools.name: cutout
tools.description: Free picture fixes on this computer for a picture already in a shot: trim its empty see-through edges, crop a percent off each side, or flip it. Give member (a cast member id with a picture) or leave it out for the shot's background picture. One undo step. Returns the new size. To remove a background (paid), use remove_background.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

member.description: A cast member id with a picture. Left out: the shot's background picture.

flip.description: true: mirror it left to right.

tools.name: upload
tools.description: Bring a file from this computer into the project, like the app's upload. Pictures (PNG/JPG/WebP/GIF/SVG): as media, character or object (joins a shot's cast or replaces a member's picture), or background. Videos (MP4/MOV/WebM): as media, video-background or video-front in a shot. Sounds (MP3/WAV/M4A...): as sound (sound Media, and on the timeline at `at` if given), music, or voice. Default: media for pictures and videos, sound for sounds. The file is copied into Dinoctor; the original isn't changed. One undo step. For pictures made before with Higgsfield, use put_picture.

path.description: Full path of the file on this computer.

as.description: How it goes into the project (see the description).

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

replace.description: A cast member id in that shot whose picture this replaces.

name.description: A short name for it in the project.

sound_kind.description: For as: sound, what it is (guessed from the name and length otherwise).

at.description: For as: sound, seconds into the film to place it on a free sound line.

trim.description: For a character/object picture: cut its empty see-through edges (default true).

tools.name: script
tools.description: The film's script, the way Sound and script does it. action get (read-only): title, the chosen voice, every line (id, text, feeling, whether it has a voice and how long) and which shots speak it; use the line ids with assign, speak or own_voice. action write: put a script in: your own lines (short, 5-15 words, one shot each), or text (a whole script, cut into lines at sentences), or only a topic (Dinoctor's Claude writes it; uses the person's own Claude Code and can take a few minutes, so say so first). Unless put_in_film is false, lines go into a scene: shots there without a voice take lines in order, and each line left over becomes a new shot sized to it. Captions show a line's words until it has a voice. replace: false adds to the script. action assign: give one shot (shot_id, or scene + shot; default the shot on screen) one line: the shot speaks that line's voice (or shows its words as a caption until it has one), replacing its own voice; fit: true makes the shot as long as the line. write and assign are one undo step each. To make the voices, call speak next.

action.description: get the script, write lines into it, or assign one line to one shot.

lines.description: write: your own lines, in order: plain strings or { text, feeling }.

text.description: write: a whole script to cut into lines at sentences.

topic.description: write: only a topic: Dinoctor's Claude writes the script.

seconds.description: For a topic: how long the film is (default 60).

tone.description: For a topic: the tone, like 'funny' or 'calm documentary'.

replace.description: false: add to the script instead of replacing it. Default true.

put_in_film.description: false: only keep the lines in the script, don't touch shots. Default true.

scene.description: write: the scene to put the lines in, index from 0 (default: the scene on screen). assign: with shot, the shot's scene.

new_shots.description: false: leftover lines wait instead of becoming new shots.

fit.description: Shots that take a line get the line's length (write: default true; assign: default false).

captions.description: Show captions of the lines (default true).

line.description: assign: a line id from action get.

shot_id.description: assign: the shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

tools.name: voices
tools.description: List the ElevenLabs voices in the person's own account (id, name, what it sounds like), read-only. With pick: a voice id becomes the film's voice for speak (one undo step). Needs ElevenLabs connected (see generator_account). Making voices costs characters: that's speak.

pick.description: A voice id from the list to make it the film's voice.

tools.name: speak
tools.description: Make the voice for script lines with ElevenLabs, with the time of every word, and give it to the shots that speak each line (captions follow the words; shots fit the voice unless fit is false). Spends the person's ElevenLabs characters: the first call (without confirm) returns the cost and what's left; ask, then call again with confirm: true. Default: every line without a voice, in the film's voice. Returns what was made and characters left. For the person's own recording (free), use own_voice.

lines.description: Line ids from script with action get. Default: every line without a voice.

voice.description: An ElevenLabs voice id (voices). Default: the film's voice.

model.description: Default eleven_multilingual_v2. Flash and turbo cost half.

again.description: Make the voice again even for lines that have one.

fit.description: Shots get the voice's length (default true).

confirm.description: true only after the person agreed to the cost.

tools.name: own_voice
tools.description: Use the person's own recording (a sound file on this computer) as a voice, free: for a script line (line), for a shot (it becomes that shot's line), or as a new line. Its words are heard on this computer when voice text is set up, so captions can follow them. cut_pauses takes out long pauses. One undo step. For an AI voice (paid) use speak; for music use music.

path.description: Full path of the sound file (MP3, WAV, M4A...).

line.description: A line id (script with action get) that this recording speaks.

shot_id.description: Or: a shot's id; the recording becomes that shot's line. Or give scene and shot.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

fit.description: true: the shot gets the recording's length.

tools.name: music
tools.description: The film's background music: add the person's music file (it's levelled so it sits under the voice; the levelled copy replaces it by itself a minute or two later), set its volume and how far it drops under the voice, or remove it. One undo step. Returns the music settings. For short sounds at a moment, use upload as sound or sound_effects.

path.description: Full path of a music file on this computer.

name.description: A name for it. Default: the file name.

duck.description: How far it drops under the voice, dB 0 to 24. Default 12.

tools.name: sound_effects
tools.description: Dinoctor's automatic sound effects (from the style's sound pack, worked out from what happens in each shot). Film-wide: on, volume, room tone. One shot: shot_on, shot_volume, and one sound by its event key: event_on, pick another sound, own_path (the person's own file), gain, nudge, reset. Call with just the shot (shot_id, or scene + shot) to list that shot's sounds and their event keys (no change). One undo step per change. For music use music; for any other sound file use upload as sound.

on.description: Film-wide: sound effects on or off.

room.description: Film-wide: quiet room tone under everything.

shot_id.description: A shot's id (or give scene and shot). With only this, lists the shot's sounds.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

shot_on.description: This shot's sound effects on or off.

event.description: One sound's event key, from the list.

pick.description: Another sound from that event's choices.

own_path.description: Full path of the person's own sound file to use for that event.

reset.description: true: that sound back to automatic.

tools.name: my_styles
tools.description: Read-only: the person's own art styles (ones Claude built for them in Dinoctor) with id, name, a short about, tokens used and their star rating, plus the style job running now (building or fixing, with progress). Use an id with use_style, style_job (action fix), rate_style or delete_style. Built-in styles are listed by list_styles.

tools.name: style_job
tools.description: Build, fix and follow the person's own art styles: Claude Code runs inside Dinoctor and does the work. Only one style job runs at a time. action build: start a brand-new style from words and/or example pictures (name, words, files), the same as "Build your own style". Claude Code runs inside Dinoctor on this computer and builds the style in code: it plans the look, draws characters, objects and places, writes the style, runs the app's tests, checks a test shot and makes the pictures. Usually about 30 minutes (longer for a detailed 3D style), and it uses a lot of the person's own Claude usage (a smaller plan can hit its limit). Nothing is paid to Dinoctor. The person can keep working, and style_job with action cancel stops it at any time. Claude first writes a plan; when status shows status plan, show it to the person and answer it with action continue. action fix: ask Claude to fix a problem (words) in one of the person's own finished styles (id), like Fix a problem (about 10 minutes of their Claude usage); the style stays as it was until the fix passes. action continue: answer a new style's plan (build it, or send change to rework it), or resume a build or fix that stopped part way (status says canContinue: true). build, fix and continue use the person's Claude usage, so the first call only says what will happen; ask, then call again with the same arguments and confirm: true. action status (read-only unless close: true, which clears a finished job from Dinoctor's screen): status (running, plan, done, failed, cancelled), step, what Claude does now, minutes so far and left, tokens, errors. action cancel: stops the running job; the person's styles stay as they were. When done, use_style switches to it and rate_style records how it went.

action.description: build a new style, fix one, continue a plan or a stopped job, cancel the running job, or get its status.

name.description: build: the style's name, up to 30 characters.

words.description: build: the look (characters, world, mood, lettering), needed unless files are sent. fix: what's wrong, in plain words.

files.description: build: full paths of pictures or short videos on this computer that show the look (up to 25 MB each). They show Claude far more than words.

use_project_files.description: build: also send the files already added in Dinoctor's Build your own box.

id.description: fix: The person's own style id from my_styles (built-in styles can't be used here).

change.description: continue, when status shows a plan: what the person wants changed. With it, Claude rewrites the plan instead of building.

close.description: status: clear a finished, failed or cancelled job from Dinoctor's screen.

confirm.description: build, fix, continue: true starts it (uses the person's Claude usage). Only after the person said yes.

tools.name: rate_style
tools.description: Save the person's rating of one of their own styles (1 to 5 stars and a comment), as Dinoctor asks after a build or fix. Only rate with what the person told you; never make up a rating. It stays on this computer. Returns { rated, stars }.

id.description: The person's own style id from my_styles (built-in styles can't be used here).

comment.description: The person's own words about it.

tools.name: delete_style
tools.description: Delete one of the person's own styles for good. It can't be undone, and templates in that style stop opening. Without confirm: true it only says what will go; ask the person first. Dinoctor reloads afterwards. Built-in styles can't be deleted. To only stop using it, switch with use_style instead.

id.description: The person's own style id from my_styles (built-in styles can't be used here).

confirm.description: true only after the person said to delete it.

tools.name: use_style
tools.description: Switch the project to another art style, a built-in id (list_styles) or one of the person's own (my_styles). Every shot is rebuilt in the new style: its characters, objects and places are replaced; words, cameras and timing stay. One undo step, and no confirm step, so ask the person first if the project has work. A style built since Dinoctor opened makes the window reload once. For built-in styles with a confirm step, set_style does the same.

id.description: A style id from list_styles or my_styles.

tools.name: samples
tools.description: Ready-made samples in the current style: whole films and shot runs (on shelves like "Whole films", "Film openings", "Hooks"), shot recipes (groups like "Big scenes", "Instagram hook"), and samples the person saved. action list (read-only; shelf or search narrows it), open (plays one in the preview without adding it; returns its shots and the pictures it needs), close, add (puts its shots in: how add = after the shot, shot = in place of the shot, scene = over the whole scene; returns new shot ids and picture spots to fill), needs (empty picture spots; fill them with fill_spot), save (saves a scene's shots as the person's own sample). Adding is one undo step. For single ids (a camera, an action) use library; for whole saved projects use templates.

id.description: A sample id (or exact name) from list.

search.description: For list: words to look for.

how.description: For add: add = after the shot, shot = in place of the shot, scene = over the whole scene.

group.description: For needs: the group returned by add.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

tools.name: fill_spot
tools.description: Put a picture into an empty picture spot a sample is waiting for (a stand-in person, a photo, a screen or a card's picture). key comes from samples "needs" or "add". Send a picture file from this computer (full path), or the address of a picture Dinoctor already has (starting with /, as generate or upload tools return). One undo step. To put a picture into a shot's cast or background instead, use upload or put_picture.

key.description: The spot's key from samples "needs" or "add".

file.description: Full path of a png, jpg or webp.

url.description: Or: a Dinoctor picture address starting with /.

tools.name: templates
tools.description: The person's templates (saved whole projects to start from), like Dinoctor's Templates page. action list (read-only), save (name: saves the project as it is now), open (id: replaces the open project with the template; one undo step brings it back), delete (id: for good, needs confirm: true after the person agrees). For .dino project files use open_project / save_project; for shot recipes use samples.

id.description: A template id from list (open, delete).

confirm.description: For delete: true only after the person agreed.

tools.name: draw
tools.description: Draw a new character, object or place yourself, free, in the current style's own format, and add it to the person's library: a character or object also joins the shot's cast, a place becomes the shot's place (add_to_shot: false only saves it). Use it for simple things the style doesn't have; for a photo-like picture use generate_picture (paid). No Claude usage or credits are spent: you send the drawing as plain data and Dinoctor checks it (bad fields are dropped; a drawing that fails is refused with the reason). action draw (default) sends the drawing; action describe (read-only) returns the exact format for that kind in the current style (or style), with the look the style wants and an example when it has one: read it before drawing. Formats in short: Pixel = {"name","rows":["..##..",...],"colors":{"#":"#535353"}} (up to 28x28, '.' empty; a character also has "eyes":[[col,row]],"mouth":[col,row], faces right and is at least 20 columns wide); Toon character = {"name","skin","shirt","pants","hair":"tuft|bob|ears|antennae|cap|horns|none","hairColor","snout","tail","wide","tall"}, Toon object = {"name","w","h","shapes":[{"type":"rect|ellipse|poly","x","y","w","h","color","points"}]} (y up is negative, stands on y 0); Voxel = {"name","boxes":[{"at":[x,y,z],"size":[w,h,d],"color"}]} (a character's boxes also have "part":"body|legL|legR|armL|armR", plus "eyes","mouth","faceZ"); other styles have their own format (action describe). Places in every style: {"name","sky","horizon","floor","dark","stars","clouds","orb","items":[{"kind","x","z","size"}]}. Returns the new id. Then use look_at_shot to check it.

action.description: draw (default) sends a drawing; describe returns the format to use.

drawing.description: draw: ONE drawing object in the style's format (not an array).

add_to_shot.description: draw: false only saves it to the library. Default true: a character or object joins the shot's cast, a place becomes the shot's place.

shot_id.description: The shot's id from get_project. Or give scene and shot instead. Left out: the shot on screen.

scene.description: Scene index from 0 (with shot). Used when shot_id isn't given.

shot.description: Shot index from 0 inside that scene (with scene; alone: in the scene on screen). A shot id works here too.

x.description: draw, character or object: left to right, about -6 to 6. Empty spaces it automatically.

size.description: draw, character or object: 1 is normal.

style.description: describe: a style id. Default: the project's style.

instructions: Dinoctor is a video app where you direct animated videos: a project has scenes, a scene has shots, and a shot has a place, a cast of characters and objects, actions, text, a camera move, lighting and a transition. Start with open_dinoctor, then get_project. Use library to see what each style offers before choosing ids. Name a shot with shot_id, or scene and shot indexes (left out: the shot on screen). After changes, use look_at_shot to see the shot and fix what's wrong. Tools that spend the person's credits return a price first and need confirm: true; always ask the person before confirming.
